channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: India Gold price today: Gold falls, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Gold prices fell in India on Friday, according to data compiled by FXStreet.

item.title: RBI keeps repo rate unchanged in June: What 5.25% means for the Indian Rupee
item.description: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) decided to keep the repo rate unchanged at 5.25% after concluding the June monetary policy meeting on Friday. The decision aligned with the market expectations.

item.title: EUR/JPY Price Forecast: Remains close to 186.00 near descending channel top
item.description: EUR/JPY moves little after posting modest gains in the previous day, trading around 185.80 during the Asian hours on Friday. The EUR/JPY cross is holding a constructive bullish bias as it remains above both the nine-day and 50-day Exponential Moving Averages (EMAs).

item.title: Nonfarm Payrolls set to show broadly stable US job market as Fed rate hike odds mount
item.description: The United States (US) Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) will release the Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) data for May on Friday at 12:30 GMT.

item.title: United States Dollar Index wobbles around 99.40 in countdown to US NFP data
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) struggles for a direction as investors await the United States (US) Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) data for May, which will be published at 12:30 GMT.

item.title: Gold falls on stalled US-Iran ceasefire talks, US NFP data looms
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) attracts some sellers to near weekly low during the Asian session on Friday. The precious metal remains volatile amid ongoing geopolitical turmoil. Traders will closely monitor the developments surrounding the US-Iran peace deal and the US May employment report later on Friday.

item.title: 17-year lows: South Korean Won in a downward spiral
item.description: USD/KRW extends its five-day winning streak, trading around 1,540 after hitting 1,549, a level previously seen in March 2009, during the Asian hours on Friday. The South Korean Won continues to decline despite explicit pledges from government officials to curb excessive market volatility.

item.title: Oman’s Mina al Fahal terminal halts Oil loading after alleged drone attack – Reuters
item.description: Citing two people familiar with the matter, Reuters reported on Friday that Oman’s Mina al Fahal terminal has halted crude oil loading, following an explosion near its single-buoy mooring (SBM) berths.

item.title: Canadian Dollar draws support from higher oil prices
item.description: USD/CAD depreciates after two days of gains, trading around 1.3900 during the Asian hours on Friday. The pair declines as the commodity-linked Canadian Dollar (CAD) gains support from rising oil prices.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD plummets below $72.50 ahead of US NFP data
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) is down 2% to near $72.40 during the Asian trading session on Friday.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar declines amid facing US tariff threats
item.description: NZD/USD loses ground after posting minor gains in the previous day, trading around 0.5850 during the Asian hours on Friday. The currency pair depreciated as the New Zealand Dollar (NZD) struggled against potential trade headwinds.

item.title: Australian Dollar loses ground below 0.7150 despite hawkish RBA stance
item.description: The AUD/USD pair loses momentum to around 0.7120 during the early Asian session on Friday. The Australian Dollar (AUD) softens against the US Dollar (USD) amid a cautious mood and ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The US May employment report will be in the spotlight later on Friday.

item.title: Japanese Yen gains amid intervention threats
item.description: USD/JPY extends its losses for the second successive day, trading around 159.90 during the Asian hours on Friday. The currency pair depreciated as the Japanese Yen (JPY) found support from heightened fears of government intervention.

item.title: PBOC sets USD/CNY reference rate at 6.8157 vs. 6.8203 previous
item.description: The People’s Bank of China (PBOC) sets the USD/CNY central rate for the trading session ahead on Friday at 6.8157 compared to the previous day's fix of 6.8203 and 6.7735 Reuters estimate.

item.title: Euro flatlines as traders await US jobs report
item.description: The EUR/USD pair holds steady around 1.1620 during the early Asian session on Friday. Traders prefer to wait on the sidelines ahead of the key US economic data. The US jobs data for May will be the highlight later in the day.

item.title: WTI declines below $91.00 despite Iran threats
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI), the US crude oil benchmark, is trading around $90.85 during the early Asian trading hours on Friday. The WTI price trades with mild losses as traders continue to assess the developments surrounding the US-Iran peace deal.

item.title: Japan’s Katayama says always ready to react suitably as needed on forex
item.description: Japan’s Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said on Friday that the authorities are always ready to react suitably as needed on foreign exchange.

item.title: US President Donald Trump says he could meet Iran’s supreme leader ‘if it was to make a deal’
item.description: US President Donald Trump said that he would be “honored” to meet Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei if a deal is reached to end the U.S.-Iran war, CNBC reported on Thursday.

item.title: British Pound Sterling leans on hikes its economy can't justify
item.description: Sterling is standing on a bet that gets harder to justify by the week. Markets still lean toward Bank of England (BoE) rate hikes this year, even as the economy beneath the Pound flashes contraction rather than the overheating that would normally warrant tighter policy.

item.title: Aussie Dollar stuck as the RBA talks tough into a slowdown
item.description: The Australian Dollar is going nowhere in a hurry, and the contradiction at its core explains why. The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) keeps dangling the prospect of another hike, yet the economy it governs just expanded 0.3% in the first quarter, a clear step down from the prior pace.

item.title: Japanese Yen coiled at the line, leaning on everyone but Japan
item.description: The Yen is doing very little, and that stasis is the whole story.

item.title: Euro grinds higher as jobless claims clip USD before NFP
item.description: The Euro registers modest gains of 0.12% as traders remain optimistic about the outcome of US-Iran talks, which had been uninterrupted, as revealed by the Pakistani Foreign Minister to journalist Mallick.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah: Policy risks and energy shock pressure IDR – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad reports USD/IDR has hit a fresh record high above 18,000, while Indonesian equities have slumped to multi-year lows.

item.title: NZD/USD stays muted as markets monitor Iran developments
item.description: The NZD/USD pair trades near the 0.5870 level on Friday, as the United States Dollar (USD) remains supported by cautious Federal Reserve (Fed) commentary and safe-haven demand amid ongoing uncertainty surrounding Iran.

item.title: Singapore Dollar Further losses capped by 1.2855 versus dollar – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note that USD/SGD has broken to a two‑month high near 1.2840, with strong momentum pointing to further Dollar strength against the Singapore Dollar.

item.title: Forex Today: Investors look ahead to US NFP report
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) fell toward 99.18 early Thursday before steadily climbing during the North American session to 99.45 as investors digested comments from a series of Federal Reserve (Fed) officials ahead of the highly anticipated Nonfarm Payrolls report on Friday.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah: Tight liquidity and policy risks weigh versus US Dollar – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lloyd Chan highlights that IDR is under particular pressure as rising US yields intersect with domestic policy uncertainty and higher energy prices.

item.title: Vietnam Dong: Inflation and trade headwinds build – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank highlights that Vietnam’s May Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose to 5.6% year-on-year, the highest since January 2020, driven by food and energy costs, while the trade deficit widened to a record USD 5.2 billion on strong import growth.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG rebounds, capped below 50-day SMA as bears hold grip
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) price bounces off weekly lows at $72.46 on Thursday, trading near $74.00, up over 1.70% on the day, as market mood is mixed, with investors rotating out of technology stocks and into other sectors, even though tensions around the Middle East conflict remain high.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Neutral within defined band against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann report a sharp rebound in USD/CNH above 6.78, which invalidated their prior bearish view. They now see the pair as neutral, expecting consolidation between 6.7620 and 6.7980 near term, with 6.7850 and 6.7980 acting as key resistance levels.
